::: {.callout-warning}
## Before you connect anything

The generator's output is bipolar and can swing well outside $0$–$3.3$ V; it
must **never** reach the analog input pin directly. Build and verify the
conditioning stage first, on the bench, with a DMM — not with the board
connected — and confirm its output stays inside $[V_\mathrm{lo}, V_\mathrm{hi}]$
for the full range of amplitudes you intend to use, before the first wire
goes to a pin. See [Before you connect anything](../S1-daq-static/handbook.qmd#sec-s1-hardware)
in S1 for the same warning about pin tolerances, which applies here
unchanged.
:::

### 1. Build and verify the conditioning stage {#sec-s3-step-condition}

```bash
arduino-io list
arduino-io info
```

Using @eq-s3-gain-offset, compute $G$ and $V_\mathrm{off}$ for your generator's
amplitude setting and your chosen headroom against the board's
$V_\mathrm{io}$. Build the stage described in
[the conditioning board](../../hardware/conditioning-board.qmd), then, with
the generator set to a **static** (0 Hz, DC) output at each of its extremes,
measure the conditioning stage's output with the DMM and confirm it lands
inside $[V_\mathrm{lo}, V_\mathrm{hi}]$ — not just close, inside.

Record the DMM readings against the design targets. A discrepancy here is the
conditioning stage's own gain and offset error, and it is the first two
components of the uncertainty budget in @sec-s3-budget — measure it before
you need it.

::: {.callout-tip}
## No conditioning board yet?

The [reference data](index.qmd#sec-s3-index-data) models the same stage
numerically —
gain and offset applied before the S1 ADC model — so every analysis task
below runs against it unmodified. Build the hardware when it is available and
repeat the tasks with your own runs; nothing in the templates changes.
:::

### 2. The aliasing sweep {#sec-s3-step-sweep}

Set the sampling rate deliberately low and sweep the generator's frequency
through it, well below *and* well above the Nyquist frequency $f_s/2$, taking
one recording per frequency:

```bash
arduino-io mode 15 analog
# generator set to f = 35 Hz
arduino-io stream 15 --hz 500 --seconds 2 --csv data/alias-f0035.csv
# generator set to f = 95 Hz, repeat, and so on
```

Choose enough frequencies, on both sides of $f_s/2$ and past $f_s$, that
several different values of $k = \operatorname{round}(f/f_s)$ occur — the
shipped reference data uses 16 frequencies from 35 Hz to 935 Hz at
$f_s = 500$ Hz (Nyquist 250 Hz), giving $k = 0, 1, 2$. Write down the
generator's own frequency setting in each sidecar
(`channels[].generator_frequency_hz`) — that is the ground truth
@eq-s3-alias is checked against, and it does not appear anywhere else in the
file.

::: {.callout-important}
## Do not compute $f_a$ at the bench

Write down $f$ as set on the generator, and nothing else. Computing the
predicted alias by hand and writing *that* down instead removes the point of
the comparison in the analysis template — you would be checking your own
arithmetic, not the acquisition.
:::

### 3. Anti-alias filter: with and without {#sec-s3-step-filter}

Pick one frequency clearly above $f_s/2$ — the shipped data uses 650 Hz at
$f_s = 500$ Hz, which folds to 150 Hz — and record it twice: once straight
into the conditioning stage, once through
[the filter stage](../../hardware/filter-stage.qmd) ahead of the
conditioning stage.

```bash
# generator at 650 Hz, filter stage bypassed
arduino-io stream 15 --hz 500 --seconds 2 --csv data/filter-off.csv
# generator at 650 Hz, filter stage in circuit
arduino-io stream 15 --hz 500 --seconds 2 --csv data/filter-on.csv
```

Record the filter's corner frequency and order in the sidecar
(`channels[].filter_fc_hz`, `channels[].filter_order`, and a human-readable
description in `conditioning.filter`) for the filtered run; leave
`conditioning.filter: none` for the unfiltered one. Both runs are otherwise
identical — same generator frequency, same amplitude, same sampling rate —
so any difference between them is the filter's doing and nothing else's.

### 4. An oversampled run, for the digital-filtering section {#sec-s3-step-oversample}

Set the generator to output two tones at once — a 150 Hz signal and a much
higher-frequency interferer — and sample fast enough that neither one is
anywhere near $f_s/2$:

```bash
arduino-io stream 15 --hz 5000 --seconds 1 --csv data/oversampled.csv
```

If your generator cannot sum two tones, record them as two separate
oversampled runs at the same $f_s$ and add the columns in the analysis
template instead; note which approach you used in `environment.notes`.

### 5. Fill the sidecars {#sec-s3-step-sidecar}

Every run needs, beyond the fields S1 already asks for
(the [same checklist as S1](../S1-daq-static/handbook.qmd#sec-s1-step-sidecar)):

- [ ] `channels[].conditioning.gain` and `.offset` — the values **actually
      measured** in step 1, not the design targets from @eq-s3-gain-offset
- [ ] `channels[].generator_frequency_hz` — the generator's own setting, for
      every run
- [ ] `channels[].filter_fc_hz`, `channels[].filter_order` and a description
      in `conditioning.filter` — for the filtered run of @sec-s3-step-filter
      only; `conditioning.filter: none` for every other run
- [ ] `channels[].reference_value` and `.reference_u` — the generator's peak
      amplitude and its uncertainty, from the generator's own specification
- [ ] `synthetic: false`

These are S3-specific extensions of the channel schema in
[Data format](../../data-format/index.qmd#sec-fields); the general fields
there (`pin`, `quantity`, `unit`, …) are unchanged.
